methodological_rigor.justification: This is a prespecified exploratory multiomic substudy of the CITN-12 phase 1 trial (NCT02595866) in 30 PLWH with cancer, integrating bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, plasma cytokines, flow cytometry, HIV DNA/RNA quantification, and in vitro HIV challenge across pre-defined timepoints (C01D01, C01D02, C01D08, EOT). Analytic pipeline is solid: GSEA with BH correction, LASSO with leave-one-out CV, MAST for scRNA-seq DE, ComBat batch correction across two RNA-seq batches, CIBERSORT deconvolution cross-validated against flow, ridge regression with reported ρ=0.59 (P=0.035), NicheNet for ligand inference, and SCimilarity mapping to an external reference. Statistical choices (Wilcoxon matched-pairs, Mann-Whitney, Friedman+Dunn, Spearman) are appropriate for the small n and paired design; however, limitations are material — no randomization, no HIV-negative comparator, n=14 at EOT with group-2 n=5, group assignment derived from the outcome variable (HIV DNA at EOT), and authors explicitly note no sample size justification, no blinding, no intact proviral DNA assay (IPDA), and no tissue sampling, which the discussion acknowledges.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual prospective longitudinal cohort/exploratory substudy of an open-label non-randomized phase 1 trial, placing it at Oxford 2b. Clinical relevance is direct and translational: the work identifies a preexisting IFN/ISG-high, low-TGFβ, low-Treg baseline signature that predicts HIV reservoir decay under pembrolizumab in PLWH with cancer, proposes actionable biomarker-based patient selection, and motivates combination strategies with type I IFN agonists, TLR agonists, IL-15 superagonists, or TGFβ inhibitors — including an in vitro validation showing IFN/TLR agonists restrict HIV infection. While compelling and hypothesis-generating, findings are not yet practice-changing, hinge on small group sizes (9 vs 5 at EOT), and require validation in larger homogeneous cohorts before influencing cure-strategy guidelines.

reporting_quality.justification: As a prospective observational multiomic substudy of a registered phase 1 trial, STROBE is the most appropriate reporting standard (TRIPOD partially applies to the ridge model). Reporting is thorough: trial registration (NCT02595866) and IRB approvals across multiple centers are stated, participant selection and cohort stratification are detailed, timepoints and assay availability are tabulated (Supplementary Data 1, D3), statistical tests are specified per figure, software versions (FlowJo 10.8.1/10.10.0, GraphPad 10.2.3, R 4.4.0) are disclosed, and a Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary is referenced. Limitations (no IPDA, no tissue, no sex-stratified analysis, no power calculation) are explicitly acknowledged. Data availability is strong: RNA-seq to be deposited on GEO, and code/data on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.11200738), though the GEO accession is noted as pending upon publication which prevents a perfect score.

novelty_literature.justification: The manuscript makes a novel mechanistic contribution by dissecting — at single-cell, bulk-transcriptomic, proteomic, and functional levels — a 24-hour innate-antiviral ISG/TLR program coupled to myeloid-T cell crosstalk that stratifies HIV reservoir decay after anti-PD-1 in a population (PLWH with cancer) rarely studied in depth. The identification of a preexisting ISGhi/low-WNT/low-Treg baseline state predictive of reservoir reduction, its generalization via SCimilarity across ~1,000 public datasets, and the in vitro demonstration that IFN/TLR agonists restrict HIV infection (abrogated by IFNAR/IFNγ blockade) together constitute a meaningful conceptual advance beyond prior CITN-12 reports by Uldrick et al. (refs 27, 30). Guarding against novelty leniency: the core clinical trial and its virologic endpoints were previously published, PD-1 blockade effects on HIV have been reported in ex vivo and NHP work (refs 22–30), and the 36% overlap with the DURVAST signature is explicitly acknowledged, so this is a rigorous extension rather than first-in-class discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: Writing is clear, technically precise, and well-organized across abstract, methods, results, and discussion, with a logical arc from bulk transcriptomics to single-cell resolution to in vitro mechanistic validation. Figure legends (Figs. 1–6) are unusually detailed and explicitly describe statistics, sample sizes per panel, and color encoding; abbreviations are defined on first use (PLWH, ISG, TLR, SLEA, etc.). Minor issues include heavy acronym density that occasionally impairs readability, a discussion that ventures into combination-therapy speculation, and an apparent typo ('PEMPA1' for PMEPA1) in the TGFβ signaling gene list. Overall the manuscript is publication-ready in presentation.

key_strengths: Prospective multi-site phase 1 trial (CITN-12, NCT02595866) leveraging longitudinal matched bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, plasma cytokines, flow cytometry, and HIV DNA/RNA assays with prespecified timepoints

Identification of a preexisting ISGhi/TLR-high, low-WNT/Treg baseline signature that stratifies reservoir decay (median 2.39-fold HIV DNA reduction in group 1) and is validated across ~1,000 public single-cell datasets via SCimilarity
Mechanistic closure via in vitro HIV challenge in 5 donors showing IFNα/IFNγ/poly I:C/R848 restrict infection and that IFNAR+IFNγ blockade abrogates protection
Rigorous statistics: BH correction, LASSO LOOCV, ComBat batch correction, ridge regression with reported ρ and P, NicheNet ligand inference, CIBERSORT cross-validated against flow cytometry
Strong reporting and reproducibility commitments including Zenodo code/data deposition (10.5281/zenodo.11200738) and pending GEO upload
key_concerns: Small EOT cohort (n=14; group 1 n=9, group 2 n=5) with groups defined using the outcome variable (HIV DNA at EOT), raising circularity/overfitting risk for the stratification claims
No randomization, no HIV-negative or untreated control arm, no power calculation, and authors were not blinded — acknowledged but limits causal inference on PD-1 as the driver of the signature
Absence of Intact Proviral DNA Assay (IPDA) and tissue sampling means replication-competent and tissue-resident reservoir dynamics cannot be directly assessed
Sex imbalance (29 male, 1 female) precludes sex-stratified analyses and limits generalizability; 11 heterogeneous cancer types further confound mechanistic attribution

Ridge model predictive performance (ρ=0.59, P=0.035) is modest and not validated in an independent holdout cohort; SCimilarity generalizability claims rest on unsupervised similarity mapping rather than prospective testing
chief_reviewer.rationale: The manuscript delivers a methodologically solid, mechanistically integrated, and clinically motivated multiomic substudy of a registered phase 1 trial in an underserved population (PLWH with cancer), with in vitro confirmation and external generalization. Given the novelty of the 24-hour innate-antiviral stratifier, the integrated bulk+single-cell+functional design, and publication-ready presentation — set against small group sizes and outcome-derived stratification — the paper is plausible for a tier-1 venue (e.g., Nature Medicine/Nature Cancer class) with minor revisions to clarify circularity, add external validation detail, and finalize GEO deposition.
